stories.headline: Trumbull Veterans and First Responders Center enters final construction phase
stories.summary: VFW Post 10059’s 5,500-square-foot Veterans and First Responders Center in Trumbull is in its final construction phase after nearly a decade of planning, pandemic delays, and a $900,000 state grant. The multi-use hub will serve veterans, first responders, small businesses, and residents of Trumbull, Shelton, Monroe, Easton, and Redding, with completion targeted by year-end. Recent private gifts totaling $35,000 added a generator and a Wall of Honor near the entrance.

stories.headline: DOJ ramps up noncitizen voting prosecutions ahead of November midterms
stories.summary: The Justice Department has charged about 20 people this month under the federal “voting by aliens” statute — roughly 13% of all such cases since the law was enacted — and 32 in the last four weeks, Reuters reports. DHS has mobilized agents in all 50 states, calling the work a White House “tier-one priority,” while critics say the push erodes public trust despite studies showing noncitizen voting is rare. A separate Reuters review found states may have added more than 30,000 self-declared noncitizens to rolls since 2000 through software and clerical errors.

stories.headline: AP: U.S. citizen left bloodied after ICE agents mistook him for a fugitive
stories.summary: A U.S. citizen was injured and hospitalized Sunday in Evanston, Illinois, after ICE agents mistook him for a fugitive, refused his ID demands turned into a struggle, then released him once they confirmed he was not their target. Witnesses told AP agents pinned the man — who yelled he was a citizen — and left blood on his shirt and face; DHS said he was “not cooperative” and that officers left without further incident. Evanston police are investigating as Illinois officials condemn the encounter amid record ICE arrest numbers.

stories.headline: Kirk family notice of claim hinges on UVU chief’s ‘I got you covered’ text
stories.summary: Charlie Kirk’s family filed a notice of claim against Utah, Utah Valley University, and officials alleging rooftop-security failures before his Sept. 10, 2025 assassination. Attorneys highlight an alleged UVU Police Chief Jeffrey Long text — “I got you covered” — after TPUSA organizers raised rooftop-access concerns, arguing reliance on that assurance may help pierce Utah’s governmental immunity. The notice says no officer was on the rooftop and camera feeds were not watched in real time; Tyler Robinson has pleaded not guilty to aggravated murder.

stories.headline: ICE shooting lawyer deletes post joking about Charlie Kirk’s neck wound
stories.summary: Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, attorney for Venezuelan DoorDash driver Wilber Garces Perez shot by ICE in Austin, deleted a social post asking “How do you resist getting shot in the neck? Does Charlie Kirk have any advice on that?” Conservatives including Nancy Mace and Charlie Kirk Show staff called the timing grotesque; she told Fox the post “could be misconstrued” and was removed. DHS continues to defend the traffic-stop shooting while she disputes the government’s account of her client’s status and medical care.

stories.headline: Bessent: U.S. and China extend Busan trade truce through January 10
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Wednesday the United States and China agreed to extend the so-called Busan trade truce until January 10, after he met Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of President Xi Jinping’s Washington state visit. Bessent told Fox News the sides also discussed whether a broader deal was possible beyond a series of smaller steps. The extension pushes past the prior November 10 expiration as Trump hosts Xi for pomp-and-ceremony diplomacy amid trade and technology tensions.

stories.headline: Apple exploring screenless fitness band as Watch lineup rethink
stories.summary: Citing Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, MacRumors reports Apple has built prototypes of a screenless Apple Watch–style fitness band as it re-evaluates the Watch lineup for a “new era.” Screen-free trackers from Whoop, Oura, and Google have gained ground on distraction, weight, and battery life. Apple has reportedly not locked a direction — smart rings and even a circular Watch display are also under study — and a screenless band is not expected before at least 2028.

stories.headline: OpenAI: ChatGPT-in-Siri deal ‘persistently underperforming’ vs xAI suit
stories.summary: In a court filing against Elon Musk’s xAI, OpenAI said Apple’s ChatGPT integration in Siri was “persistently underperforming,” with early forecasts cut after a slow opt-in start. OpenAI argues there was never an exclusivity deal — Apple refused a two-year exclusive and later signed with Google/Gemini — and that foreclosure of rivals was de minimis. Musk’s companies dropped Apple from the suit earlier this month; OpenAI wants xAI’s remaining claims tossed before a January 2027 trial.

stories.headline: Jets: Aaron Glenn’s Motor City reunion vs Dan Campbell and No. 1 defense
stories.summary: For the first time as Jets head coach, Aaron Glenn returns to Detroit to face former boss Dan Campbell after four seasons as Lions defensive coordinator. New York’s defense ranks No. 1 overall and top-five against both run and pass, holding its first two foes under 200 yards, while Detroit averages 362 yards with Goff, Gibbs, and St. Brown. Lions defensive injuries (Branch, Joseph, Maddox) and a unit allowing 10 TDs in two weeks give the Jets’ WR duo of Wilson and Mitchell a secondary to test.

stories.headline: Penguins cut nine, loan Galvas to Czechia, waive Gauthier for AHL
stories.summary: On their preseason off day, the Penguins trimmed nine players, including loaning 2026 second-rounder Tomas Galvas back to Bili Tygri Liberec in Czechia after a rocky NHL preseason debut. Goaltender Taylor Gauthier was waived for assignment to Wilkes-Barre/Scranton; most others were AHL-contract defensemen plus junior forward Carter Sanderson. Pittsburgh still had about 59 players in camp with another exhibition looming before the regular-season roster crunch.
